report.answer_text:
TikTok briefly went dark in the U.S. in January 2025, then stayed online while the Trump administration delayed enforcement of a federal divest-or-ban law. ByteDance signed a deal in December to give up control of key U.S. operations, but the deal didn’t close until January 22, 2026. (everycrsreport.com)
January–February 2025: On January 17, the Supreme Court upheld the law, which barred companies from distributing or supporting TikTok in the U.S. unless ByteDance completed a qualifying divestiture. TikTok shut off U.S. access on the evening of January 18 and restored it on January 19 after Trump promised to delay enforcement. Apple and Google didn’t restore the app to their stores until February 13. (supremecourt.gov)
September–December 2025: After several enforcement delays, Trump approved a proposed divestiture framework on September 25. On December 18, TikTok and ByteDance told employees they had signed binding agreements with Oracle, Silver Lake, and Abu Dhabi-based MGX to form a U.S. joint venture. (govinfo.gov)
When the deal closed, ByteDance kept a 19.9% stake in the majority-American-owned TikTok USDS Joint Venture. Oracle, Silver Lake, and MGX each took 15%. The venture took responsibility for U.S. user data, recommendation-algorithm security, and content moderation, while TikTok’s global business retained roles in advertising and e-commerce. U.S. users could still use the same app and see content from around the world. (axios.com)
